_about: Curated DCS store reference, keyed by the CLSID codes DCS writes into a mission's pylon table. Covers the F/A-18C, A-10C and AV-8B N/A. DCS builds its own CLSID-to-name mapping by executing Lua at load time, so it cannot be read out of the game files reliably -- three separate extraction attempts produced incomplete and, worse, mismatched names. Everything here is identified by hand from self-documenting CLSID codes and verified declarations. Anything not listed is shown as its raw CLSID and flagged as having no reference data, rather than guessed at.
_quantity_note: A rack CLSID represents more than one weapon (BRU-42_2*GBU-38 is two bombs). Where that applies, 'quantity' gives the number carried on that single pylon.

stores.name: AIM-120C AMRAAM
stores.guidance: Active radar, inertial midcourse then autonomous terminal
employment: Launch high and fast -- range scales strongly with launch altitude and Mach.
Support the shot until the missile goes active, then you are free to manoeuvre.
Shots at maximum range against a manoeuvring target are easily defeated. Closer is where kills come from.
In the Hornet, the attack format shows the shoot cue and time to active; respect the minimum abort range.

stores.name: AIM-9X Sidewinder
employment: All-aspect with a wide off-boresight capability -- it will take shots well outside the HUD field of view.
Best results inside 5 nm; long-range IR shots bleed energy and are defeated by a turn.
Uncage before launch so the seeker tracks the target rather than the boresight.

stores.name: AIM-9M Sidewinder
employment: All-aspect but the rear quarter remains by far the highest-probability shot.
Uncage the seeker and listen for the growl to confirm a good lock before firing.
Practical envelope is roughly 1-5 nm.
A CATM variant is a captive training round -- it will not launch.

stores.name: AIM-7M Sparrow
employment: You must keep the target locked and illuminated all the way to impact. Break lock and the missile is lost.
That commitment is the whole cost of the weapon -- you cannot turn away or engage another target while it flies.
Carried when AMRAAM is unavailable; treat every shot as a sustained commitment.

stores.name: GBU-31 JDAM (2000 lb)
stores.guidance: GPS with inertial backup -- no laser required
stores.role: All-weather precision attack on fixed coordinates
employment: Fire and forget. Once released you may turn away immediately.
Accuracy depends entirely on target coordinate quality -- verify the coordinates before release.
Release inside the launch acceptable region cue. From 20-25k ft it reaches roughly 12-15 nm.
Genuinely all-weather; cloud between you and the target does not matter.
The V3 variant is a BLU-109 penetrator for hardened targets; the V1 and V4 are blast-fragmentation.
stores.fuzing: Programmable. Set arming and function delay before release.

stores.name: GBU-32 JDAM (1000 lb)
stores.guidance: GPS with inertial backup -- no laser required
stores.role: All-weather precision attack on fixed coordinates
employment: Fire and forget on GPS coordinates -- turn away as soon as it is off the rail.
The 1000 lb class is the middle option: more effect than a GBU-38, less overkill than a GBU-31.
Release inside the launch acceptable region; higher and faster gives more standoff.
Verify target coordinates before release -- a JDAM will hit exactly the wrong place with perfect accuracy.
Set impact azimuth and angle where the approach geometry matters, such as a runway or a bunker face.
stores.fuzing: Programmable. Set arming and function delay before release.

stores.name: GBU-38 JDAM (500 lb)
stores.role: Precision attack with reduced collateral effect
employment: Fire and forget on coordinates. The smallest JDAM, so useful where a 2000 lb blast is unacceptable.
Multiple rounds per rack means several aimpoints in one pass -- assign each weapon its own target.
Release inside the launch acceptable region cue.
Coordinate quality is everything; confirm before release.

stores.name: GBU-54 Laser JDAM (500 lb)
employment: Can be employed as a pure GPS weapon, or with terminal laser guidance against something that moves.
Laser mode is the reason to carry it -- GPS alone cannot hit a vehicle that drives away.
In laser mode, lase through impact exactly as with a conventional laser-guided bomb.
Confirm the intended mode before release; the delivery profile differs.
stores.laser_note: Laser code applies in laser mode and must match the designating pod.

stores.name: GBU-12 Paveway II (500 lb)
stores.role: Precision attack on point targets, including moving ones
employment: Release into the glide envelope, then lase continuously through impact. Stop lasing and the bomb goes ballistic.
Typical delivery: 15-20k ft, shallow dive or level, 4-8 nm slant range.
Begin lasing roughly 8-12 seconds before impact. Lasing too early bleeds energy and can fall short.
Keep the target inside the pod's field of regard for the whole time of flight.
Cloud, smoke or dust between pod and target breaks the laser and the bomb misses.
stores.fuzing: Instantaneous for soft targets, delayed for structures.
stores.laser_note: The weapon's code must match the designating pod, whether yours or a buddy's.
requires: Targeting pod, or another aircraft lasing on your code

stores.name: BDU-50 LGB (practice)
employment: Inert practice shape with laser guidance -- scores the delivery without the warhead.
Employ exactly as a GBU-12: lase through impact.

stores.name: Mk-82 (500 lb, low drag)
employment: A 30-45 degree dive released from 8-12k ft AGL gives good accuracy with adequate frag separation.
Low-level level releases with low-drag bombs are hazardous -- you fly through your own frag pattern.
Accuracy is very sensitive to release conditions: wings level, steady G, on speed.
Ripple pairs across an area target rather than aiming singles.
stores.fuzing: Set arming delay before release; longer for penetration, shorter for surface burst.

stores.name: Mk-82 Snakeye / AIR (500 lb, high drag)
employment: The retarder opens after release and steepens the fall, so you can release low and still escape the frag.
Intended for low-level laydown deliveries.
Confirm the retarded profile is selected, or the aiming solution uses the wrong ballistics and the bombs fall long.
Markedly less accurate from medium altitude -- use low drag or guided stores from height.
stores.fuzing: Retarded arming; the ballute or fins must deploy for the profile to work.

stores.name: Mk-83 (1000 lb)
employment: Twice the warhead of a Mk-82 -- for structures and hardened surface targets rather than area work.
Dive delivery from medium altitude; the larger frag envelope demands more release altitude.
Keep the release conditions steady; ballistic accuracy is unforgiving.
stores.fuzing: Set arming delay to suit the target.

stores.name: Mk-20 Rockeye
employment: Opens at a set height and spreads shaped-charge bomblets -- you are aiming a footprint, not a point.
Effective against thin-skinned vehicles and soft targets; poor against modern armour.
Release from medium altitude in a shallow dive; wind drift across the footprint is significant.
stores.fuzing: Dispenser opening height governs the pattern.

stores.name: CBU-87 / CBU-99 CEM
stores.role: Area attack on soft targets, vehicles and personnel
employment: Combined-effects bomblets over a wide footprint. Height of function sets the pattern: lower is tighter and denser.
Release from medium altitude in a shallow dive.
Ineffective against armour and hardened targets -- use on trucks, guns, air defence sites and troops.
stores.fuzing: Proximity fuze sets the height of function.

stores.name: CBU-103 (WCMD)
stores.guidance: Inertial tail kit with wind correction
stores.role: Accurate area attack from medium/high altitude
employment: The tail kit corrects the wind drift that ruins unguided cluster accuracy, so it can be released from height above light defences.
Still a footprint weapon; height of function governs the pattern.
Preferred over the CBU-87 whenever the threat forces a higher release.

stores.name: CBU-105 (WCMD, sensor-fuzed)
employment: The skeet submunitions find vehicles individually and fire downward at the hottest part of each -- a purpose-built armour killer.
One weapon can disable several vehicles in a column.
Needs a dispersed vehicle target; wasted on infantry, buildings or empty ground.
Wind correction makes it accurate from high altitude, which keeps you above short-range defences.
stores.fuzing: Set height of function; the submunitions then work autonomously.

stores.name: BDU practice bomb
employment: Inert shape matching the ballistics of the live weapon it represents.
BDU-33 is a small spotting round; BDU-50 matches a Mk-82. HD is the retarded variant.
Useful for practising delivery profiles without expending ordnance.

stores.name: AGM-65F Maverick (IIR, anti-ship)
employment: Power the seeker up early -- imaging infrared needs cooling time before it will track.
Lock before launch, then it is fire and forget; turn away immediately.
The F carries the heavy blast-fragmentation warhead and a seeker tuned for ship-sized targets.
Handing off from the targeting pod is far quicker than hunting on the narrow missile video.

stores.name: AGM-65G/K Maverick (IIR)
stores.role: Hardened points, structures and large vehicles
employment: Cool the seeker before employment; an uncooled IIR seeker will not lock.
Lock before launch and you can turn away immediately.
Heavy penetrating warhead -- use on buildings, bunkers and bridges rather than trucks.
A TGM or CATM designation is a training round and will not fire.

stores.name: AGM-65H Maverick (CCD)
stores.guidance: Charge-coupled device (daylight TV), lock before launch
stores.role: Vehicles and point targets in daylight
employment: Daylight electro-optical seeker -- needs visual contrast on the target, so it is poor at night or in haze.
Lock before launch; fire and forget once locked.
The triple rail carries three rounds on one pylon, giving useful magazine depth for a vehicle column.
Practical launch range 6-10 nm from medium altitude, limited by the seeker resolving the target.

stores.name: AGM-65L Maverick (laser)
employment: Guides on a laser spot rather than an image, so it works against targets a seeker could not resolve.
Suited to buddy lasing and forward air controller designation -- everyone must agree the code first.
Lase from before launch through impact.
Confirm the missile's code matches the designating pod before committing to the pass.
stores.laser_note: Code must match the designating pod, yours or a buddy's.

stores.name: AGM-122 Sidearm
employment: A Sidewinder airframe with an anti-radiation seeker -- short legged, for self-defence rather than planned suppression.
Homes on an emitting radar; if the site shuts down the missile is lost, though the shutdown itself suppresses it.
You must get close, which means entering the threat ring. Weigh that against what it buys.
Best used reactively against a short-range site that has just come up.

stores.name: AGM-84D Harpoon
employment: Long-range fire and forget, launched from well outside a ship's defences.
Flies a sea-skimming profile and uses its own radar terminally -- give it a target position and launch.
Very long time of flight; deconflict with friendly shipping and other package elements first.
Confirm target identity before release. It cannot be recalled.

stores.name: AGM-84H SLAM-ER
stores.guidance: GPS/INS with imaging infrared terminal and datalink
stores.role: Long-range precision land and sea attack
employment: Very long standoff against defended targets, flown to a preplanned route.
The terminal seeker can be steered over the datalink, letting you refine the aimpoint in flight.
That control costs commitment -- you must stay within datalink range to use it.
Long time of flight; sequence it carefully against the rest of the attack.
requires: AWW-13 datalink pod for terminal control

stores.name: AGM-154C JSOW
stores.guidance: GPS/INS glide weapon with imaging infrared terminal
stores.role: Attack on defended point targets from outside the threat ring
employment: Unpowered glide weapon -- release altitude and speed set the range achieved. High and fast is essential.
Roughly 40 nm from high altitude, far less from low level.
Fire and forget on coordinates; verify them before release.
The C is a unitary penetrator for hardened point targets.
Long time of flight -- account for it when sequencing with other elements.

stores.name: ADM-141A TALD decoy
employment: A glide decoy that presents a fighter-sized radar return, drawing air defences into radiating and shooting.
Released ahead of the strike to saturate and expose the threat picture for the anti-radiation shooters.
Timing is everything -- too early and the decoys are gone before the strike arrives.
Carries no warhead. It buys attention, not damage.

stores.name: AGR-20A APKWS (laser-guided rocket)
employment: A laser guidance kit on a Hydra 70 -- precision at a fraction of a missile's cost and weight.
Seven rounds per pod, so many separate engagements per sortie against light vehicles and personnel.
Lase from launch through impact as with any laser-guided weapon.
Small warhead: right for trucks and troops, insufficient for armour or structures.
stores.laser_note: Rocket code must match the designating pod.

stores.name: Unguided rocket pod (Hydra 70 / Zuni)
employment: Unguided and widely dispersed -- an area weapon, not a precision one.
Shallow dive, fire in salvos, expect a wide pattern.
White phosphorus rounds mark targets rather than destroying them.
Firing means closing well inside short-range air defences. Weigh the threat first.

stores.name: GAU-12 Equalizer gun pod
employment: 25 mm cannon carried externally on the Harrier's centreline stations.
Fire in short bursts; the ammunition goes quickly and the barrel life is finite.
Strafe in a 10-15 degree dive, open fire around 4000 ft slant, break off by 2000 ft to stay clear of debris.
Effective against soft-skinned vehicles and personnel, not armour.

stores.name: AN/ASQ-228 ATFLIR
stores.role: Target identification, designation and laser designation
employment: Required for any laser-guided weapon you intend to designate yourself.
Set and verify the laser code on the pod before stepping; it must match your weapons.
Point track for fixed targets, area track for moving ones.
Also your best identification sensor -- use it to confirm the target before release.
stores.laser_note: This pod sets the designating code. Everything you lase uses it.

stores.name: AN/AAQ-28 LITENING
stores.role: Target identification, designation and laser designation
employment: Required for self-designated laser-guided weapons.
Verify the laser code matches your weapons before stepping.
Slave to a waypoint to find the target area quickly, then refine manually.
Use it to identify the target before release, especially under restrictive rules of engagement.
stores.laser_note: This pod sets the designating code.

stores.name: AN/AAQ-33 Sniper XR
stores.role: Long-range identification, designation and laser designation
employment: Longer identification range than earlier pods -- useful for confirming a target from outside the threat ring.
Set and verify the laser code before stepping.
Point track for fixed targets, area track for movers.
Required for any laser-guided weapon you designate yourself.
stores.laser_note: This pod sets the designating code.

stores.name: AN/ASQ-213 HARM Targeting System
employment: Detects, classifies and ranges radar emitters, driving the attack display.
Enables precise handoffs and much better awareness of the air defence picture.
Without it you are limited to pre-planned and reactive shots.

stores.name: AN/ALQ-164 ECM pod
employment: The Harrier's self-protection jammer, carried on the centreline.
Must be switched on to have any effect -- confirm it is powered before entering the threat area.
Jamming also makes you conspicuous; some crews leave it in standby until spiked.
It buys time and degrades solutions. It does not replace manoeuvring and chaff.

stores.name: AN/ALQ-184 ECM pod
employment: Jams threat radars to degrade track quality and spoil shots.
Confirm it is powered and in the right mode before entering the threat area.
Does not make you invisible -- it degrades solutions and buys time.
Still manoeuvre and use chaff; the pod is one layer, not the answer.

stores.name: AN/AWW-13 datalink pod
employment: Provides the datalink for steering a SLAM-ER or Walleye onto its aimpoint after launch.
Carrying it commits you to staying within datalink range while the weapon flies.
Without it those weapons can only be employed on their preplanned coordinates.

stores.name: External fuel tank
employment: Confirm the tanks are actually transferring rather than trapped, or you are carrying dead weight.
Tanks add drag and restrict the manoeuvring envelope -- know the limit for your configuration.
Plan to jettison before a serious engagement if fuel state allows. Empty tanks are pure drag.

stores.name: Empty station
employment: Nothing loaded on this station.
